Concierge Medicine

Concierge medicine offers a more personalized, accessible, and patient-centered approach to healthcare, designed for individuals who value convenience, privacy, and a higher level of attention from their physician. At Orange County HouseCalls, our concierge model allows patients to move away from the limitations of traditional healthcare—such as long wait times, rushed appointments, and crowded waiting rooms—and instead experience care that is thoughtful, thorough, and tailored to their individual needs.

As a concierge patient, you benefit from extended, unrushed visits with a board-certified Internal Medicine physician who takes the time to understand your full medical history, lifestyle, and health goals. This approach allows for more accurate diagnoses, proactive prevention, and personalized treatment plans that go beyond simply addressing symptoms. Our focus is on building a strong, ongoing relationship between patient and physician, ensuring continuity of care and a deeper understanding of your health over time.

Convenience is a central part of concierge medicine. With Orange County HouseCalls, you have direct access to your physician along with same-day or next-day availability for appointments. Care is delivered wherever you are most comfortable—whether at home, in your office, or within a senior living community—eliminating the need to travel or spend time in waiting rooms. This is especially valuable for busy professionals, older adults, individuals with mobility challenges, and families seeking attentive, reliable care for their loved ones.

Our concierge services also emphasize preventive care and long-term health optimization. By having more time during each visit and better access to your physician, we are able to focus on early detection of health concerns, ongoing management of chronic conditions, and lifestyle-based strategies that support overall well-being. This proactive approach can help reduce unnecessary urgent care visits, emergency room visits, and hospitalizations.

In addition, concierge medicine provides a level of flexibility and responsiveness that is difficult to achieve in traditional settings. Whether you need prompt evaluation for an acute concern, ongoing management of a chronic condition, medication adjustments, or coordination of care with specialists, our team is committed to delivering timely, high-quality service with attention to detail.

At Orange County HouseCalls, concierge medicine is about more than convenience—it is about creating a healthcare experience that is personal, efficient, and centered around you. By combining medical expertise with accessibility and individualized care, we strive to provide a higher standard of service that supports your health with the attention and respect you deserve.

Read More

Medical Weight Loss

Medical weight loss at Orange County HouseCalls offers a personalized, physician-guided approach to achieving and maintaining a healthy weight. Unlike one-size-fits-all programs or fad diets, our medical weight loss plans are tailored to each patient’s unique health profile, lifestyle, and goals. Under the supervision of a board-certified Internal Medicine physician, we take the time to evaluate underlying factors that may be contributing to weight gain, including metabolic conditions, hormonal imbalances, medications, and lifestyle habits.

Our program focuses on safe, sustainable results through a combination of clinical evaluation, individualized nutrition guidance, lifestyle modifications, and, when appropriate, evidence-based medical therapies. Patients receive ongoing support, regular follow-up, and adjustments to their plan to ensure steady progress and long-term success. This comprehensive approach not only helps with weight reduction but also improves overall health, including blood pressure, blood sugar control, energy levels, and cardiovascular risk.

Designed for busy individuals who value convenience and personalized care, our medical weight loss services can be delivered through in-home visits or telemedicine, allowing you to receive expert guidance without disrupting your daily routine. Whether your goal is to lose weight, improve your health, or prevent chronic disease, our program provides a structured, medically supervised path to help you achieve lasting results in a safe and supportive environment.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is concierge medicine covered by insurance?

Concierge membership fees are not covered by insurance. The membership fee is separate from any insurance benefits you may have. However, patients may still use their insurance for outside services such as laboratory testing, imaging, specialist visits, hospital care, and medications, depending on their individual insurance plan.

What is included in the monthly membership fee?

The monthly membership fee includes access to personalized medical care through in-office visits, telemedicine visits, and house calls when medically appropriate. Our membership is designed to provide more direct access to the physician, longer visits, and a more convenient care experience.

Do you provide house calls throughout Orange County?

Yes. Orange County House Calls provides house calls in Aliso Viejo and surrounding Orange County communities, including Irvine, Laguna Niguel, Mission Viejo, Newport Beach, Laguna Hills, Laguna Beach, Dana Point, San Juan Capistrano, and nearby areas. Availability may depend on location, scheduling, and the type of medical concern.

Is this urgent care or primary care?

Orange County House Calls provides personalized internal medicine and concierge primary care. We are not a replacement for emergency care. For serious or life-threatening symptoms, patients should call 911 or go to the nearest emergency room.

Who is a good fit for a concierge membership?

Concierge membership may be a good fit for patients who want more direct access to their doctor, longer visits, convenient scheduling, and a more personalized primary care experience. It may be especially helpful for busy professionals, older adults, patients with chronic conditions, and patients who prefer care at home.

Do I need to be sick to schedule a visit?

No. Members may schedule visits for preventive care, chronic condition management, medication review, general health concerns, and follow-up care.

Do you offer medical weight loss services?

Yes. Orange County House Calls offers personalized medical weight loss services for patients who want physician-guided support with weight management. Our approach may include a medical evaluation, review of health history, lab work when appropriate, nutrition and lifestyle guidance, and medication options when medically appropriate.

Is medical weight loss included in the concierge membership?

Yes, Medical weight loss may be discussed as part of your personalized care plan. Depending on the patient’s goals, medical history, and treatment needs, additional costs may apply for medications, labs, or outside services.

Do you prescribe weight loss medications?

Weight loss medications may be considered when medically appropriate after a physician evaluation. Not every patient is a candidate, and treatment recommendations are based on your health history, current medications, lab results, and overall weight loss goals.

Who may benefit from medical weight loss?

Medical weight loss may be helpful for patients who have struggled to lose weight on their own, have weight-related health concerns, or want a structured plan supervised by a physician. This may include patients with high blood pressure, high cholesterol, prediabetes, diabetes, or other metabolic concerns.

Welcome to

Making an Appointment

We strongly recommend making an appointment for non-emergency visits as that will greatly reduce your wait time and give you more time with your doctor. Making an appointment is simple. Call (949) 204-1334 and one of our friendly team members will gladly assist you with booking an appointment or answering any questions you may have. We ask that you call our office 24 hours in advance if you cannot keep an appointment. We will attempt to reschedule an appointment as close to the initial date as possible

What to Expect

Upon arriving at Orange County House Calls, you will be greeted by a friendly team member who will assist you in checking in for your first visit. They will provide you with the new patient paperwork and health questionnaire. We will also need to collect your insurance information, a copy of your ID, and contact information. On subsequent visits, you need only check in at the front desk and wait to be called to the examination room. Each appointment differs, and Dr. Khaneki will inform you of what to expect prior to your appointment, except in emergency cases.

Initial Examination

In most cases, an initial examination takes about an hour. Our experienced team at Orange County House Calls will ask you questions, get to know your health habits and practices, and listen to your health concerns. We will also check your vitals and ensure everything looks and sounds right. We believe in educating patients and empowering them to make good choices to improve their overall health. Dr. Khaneki will conduct a physical examination, address any symptoms you are currently experiencing, and make recommendations for necessary treatments.

Pain Concerns

Our patients' comfort and trust are of the utmost importance to us. We strive to provide as much pain relief as possible while also combatting the root causes of your pain. If you are undergoing a treatment or procedure, Dr. Khaneki will meet with you to discuss your pain tolerance and create a plan for pain management. Working together, we will treat your health concerns in a way that minimizes pain and enables you to get back on your feet.

Personalized Concierge Medical Services

Our concierge medical services are designed to provide personalized, high-quality care tailored to your specific needs. With a focus on convenience and accessibility, we offer services such as same-day appointments, comprehensive health assessments, and direct access to your physician. Whether you are managing a chronic condition or seeking preventive care, our team is here to ensure you receive exceptional medical attention when you need it most. To learn more or schedule an initial consultation, please contact our office at (949) 204-1334. For detailed information about our pricing, please follow this link: Membership

Financial Policy

Orange County House Calls is dedicated to providing high-quality medical care to families throughout the Aliso Viejo area. We understand that all patients are different in the way they handle their finances. We will work with you to find a solution that enables you to get the medical care you need, with or without insurance. Call (949) 204-1334 to ask about our different payment options, which may include cash, check, financing, and credit cards. We provide budget-friendly medical care that provides a solution to all of your general health needs.

/privacy-policy/.h1: Orange County House Calls Privacy Policy
/privacy-policy/.html:
Our Privacy Policy was last updated on December 03, 2024. Our Privacy Policy covers any information that is collected about you and your activities while visiting our website, how that information is stored, and shared. Our Privacy Policy also covers the relationships we have with third parties and how your information may be shared with them.

What type of information do we collect?

When you visit our website, we collect any information that you give us. For example, if you fill out the contact form, that information will be stored on our website and sent to the appropriate contact at our company. We may also collect information through web beacons, cookies, and other analytics that shows us how you came to view our website and whether or not it was through an advertisement. Additionally, if you share one of our web pages or blogs through your social media account, we will collect information on that activity. We may also obtain information from publicly available sources on your browsing activity and interests.

While we do not collect personally sensitive data, we may collect information on the device you are using to visit our website along with your geographic location in order to improve your user experience. From time to time, we or our partners may send a cookie or anonymous identifier to your device.

When the law requires it, we obtain a consent before collecting and storing user information.

Partners that collect information

By visiting our website, your information may also be gathered by Google since we use Google Analytics to provide us with information about our website and the visitors to it. If you reached our site through a different search engine, information might be gathered by them, as well. This information is for analytical purposes and collected automatically when visiting our site. The information is not manually transferred and if you want more information on Google's Privacy Policy, you can click here.

How the information is used

By understanding how a viewer came to visit our website and what they did there, we can improve the overall user experience of our visitors. By collecting data, we can conduct research and identify ways that we can improve. We may use it to make changes to our website in order to make it more user-friendly or to improve the content on our site. In the future, this information may be used to improve your experience specifically or to make recommendations about how we can assist you.

If you filled out a contact form, your information would be used so that our team can reach out to you via email or a phone call. Additionally, if you sign up to be on our email list, your information will be used so that we can send communication to you. We may also use your information to provide you with promotional offers or incentives to use our products and services. This may be on our website or other places across the Internet and be provided directly by us or one of our advertising partners.

With whom we share the information

When we collect information about you, it is generally used for our purposes internally. We may share information with Google or our advertising partners for the purposes described above. We may also share your information with companies that provide services and support to us, as it pertains to them fulfilling their duties. If you comment on our blog posts or engage with us on social media, your profile information will be shared along with any comments that you post – typically this is viewable by the general public.

We do not share any personal or sensitive information without your consent. However, there may be instances where we are required to share your information by law and if so, will comply as necessary.

Protecting your information

We have taken steps to protect your information by restricting the access to your information to only select employees that would need it in order to perform their job duties. We also review our collection and storage policies on a regular basis to determine if they need to be improved.

Your options

If you do not want us to contact you or if you do not want to receive our newsletters anymore, you can unsubscribe using the link at the bottom of our emails. If you do not want information collected about you and used throughout the web, from our website and others, you can opt-out by clicking the following links and going through the process.

Consumer Opt-Out

Online Behavioral Advertising Opt-Out

If you want, you can also change the settings on your browser to block all cookies. However, if you do that some of the opt-out services may no longer work.

Changes

If we update our Privacy Policy, it will be reflected here, on our website with a new effective date at the top of the page.

Website

We make every effort to ensure the accuracy, quality, ease of use, and technology of our website. Please do not hesitate to contact us with any creative suggestions or technical issues you might encounter. A list of pages included in this site is available here on our sitemap.

How to reach us

If you have questions about our Privacy Policy or how we collect, store, and share data, you can email us using the form on our https://orangecountyhousecalls.com/contact-us/ or call (949) 204-1334. We will be happy to answer your questions. Orange County House Calls is located at 15 Mareblu Ste 230A Aliso Viejo, CA 92656.

Orange County House Calls Urgent Care Services Offered

Orange County House Calls provides a wide variety of urgent care services.

We offer a wide variety of services for patients throughout the Aliso Viejo California area.

Common Visits

Our care facilities are particularly popular during the wintertime, also known as cold and flu season. These conditions are part of a larger group of viruses known as acute upper respiratory infections. Acute upper respiratory infections are contagious infections that target the nose, throat, pharynx, larynx, and bronchi. They may be either viral or bacterial.

Our care facilities also see an uptick in visits during springtime, when many seasonal allergies kick in. This is also often correlated with asthma. Both conditions often mimic the symptoms of the common cold. Allergies may cause congestion, runny nose, itchy eyes, rashes, and even breathing problems or anaphylaxis. They may be triggered by dust, pets, pollen, food, medications, and insect stings. Patients with allergic asthma have airways that are especially sensitive to certain triggers.

Furthermore, we can treat other common bacterial infections, such as urinary tract infections (UTIs) or conjunctivitis (also known as pinkeye). Such conditions can make it uncomfortable – sometimes even impossible – for patients to perform their day-to-day activities. If left untreated, these conditions may also lead to severe consequences. For instance, UTIs may cause permanent kidney damage and pinkeye may lead to vision loss.

Those suffering from food poisoning may also benefit from going to our primary care offices. This affliction is so common that the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) estimate that an average of 48 million people are affected by food poisoning per year. Around 3,000 even die from the condition. As such, it is imperative to address it immediately. Telltale signs of foodborne illness include diarrhea (sometimes bloody), abdominal pain, vomiting, weakness, fever, and chills.

Health should never take a backseat in one's life. Our care facilities can help with various common conditions, no matter how minor they may seem.

Learn more about our most common visits

General Illnesses

We can also treat general illnesses that do not seem to go away with rest and over-the-counter medication. These can include colds, flu symptoms, strep throat, mono, various types of infections upper respiratory problems to name a few.

Many patients also come into our care facility to address feelings or symptoms of general malaise. This means the patient knows they are ill without being able to pinpoint how or why. We can diagnose and treat a wide variety of infectious diseases. Some are contagious, while others are passed on zoonotically (i.e., through insects or other animals). Others, still, are caused by consuming contaminated food or water or exposure to infected organisms.

Each infectious disease has its own unique set of symptoms. However, as stated by the Mayo Clinic, some of the most common are:

  • Diarrhea
  • Fatigue
  • Fatigue
  • Fever
  • Muscle aches

In addition to watching out for the above symptoms, patients should seek medical attention immediately if they have recently been bitten by an animal, are experiencing a severe headache accompanied by fever, have been coughing for more than one week, or are experiencing swelling or a rash.

The common cold and the flu are some of the most common infectious diseases. Others, like chickenpox and measles, may be prevented by taking a vaccine. In any case, many possible causal factors can lead to infectious disease. These involve bacteria, fungi, parasites, and viruses. Direct contact, indirect contact, insect bites, and food contamination may also contribute.

Anyone can be affected by general illness, but those who are immunocompromised are more likely to be sick. This includes patients who are taking steroids or other medications that suppress the immune system, patients with HIV/AIDS, and patients with certain types of cancer or other disorders. Washing hands regularly, keeping up on vaccinations, staying home when sick, practicing proper food safety, and traveling wisely, can help prevent contracting infectious disease.

Many times, symptoms of general illness subside quickly and without problems. However, if they are long-lasting and severe enough to cause distress, patients should not hesitate to visit an urgent care facility. A physician can diagnose and treat the source of the illness. If necessary, they can also prescribe any medication to alleviate any pain or discomfort the patient may be experiencing.

Learn more about our general illness services

Injuries

You may not be able to see the damage or know the exact cause of the injury, but avoiding treatment only makes it worse. We can diagnose fractures, breaks, injuries from falls, cuts, lacerations burns, rashes and more.

Our care facilities can also treat many common injuries. These include injuries from auto accidents, slip and fall accidents, cuts and lacerations, sprains and strains, and more. Many patients often make the honest mistake of assuming that their injuries are not that serious. However, symptoms may lie dormant for longer than expected. It is always important to seek medical attention after an injury before it has the chance to get worse. Doing so also establishes a medical record for any future physicians, lawyers, or claims adjusters to reference.

It can be upsetting and intimidating to deal with an open wound. As such, it should come as no surprise that cuts and lacerations are two of the main types of injuries treated by primary care and urgent care facilities. Patients should seek immediate medical attention whenever they suffer an injury associated with bright red, spurting, or uncontrolled bleeding. Objects may also become lodged inside deep wounds, which should only be removed by a medical professional.

Car accident injuries are another popular reason to visit our facility. It is crucial for individuals to see a medical professional following an auto accident – even if they do not feel like they suffered any injuries. It is not uncommon for a cocktail of adrenaline and other protective hormones to prevent victims from feeling the full effect of their injuries until some time has passed – at which point their condition may have already worsened.

According to the National Floor Safety Institute, slip and fall accidents are so common that they are among the leading causes of lost workdays nationwide. Since the category is so broad, the results may range from a small scrape to a traumatic brain injury. Any injury that leads to a blow to the head should be checked out immediately. Along with treating more minor fall injuries, primary care physicians can treat possible concussions and refer patients out to specialists as necessary.

Finally, sprains and strains are another common cause of primary care facility visits. Patients with sprains have stretched or torn their ligaments, while those with strains have stretched or torn their tendons. Both conditions can be incredibly painful, leading to swelling and tenderness in the affected area. Severe sprains and strains may not even be able to handle weight at all. A primary care physician can evaluate these conditions, take X-rays, devise a personalized treatment plan unique to the patient's needs, and refer them out to a specialist, as necessary.

It is crucial for patients to treat any injuries right away, even if they do not feel it is necessary. As mentioned earlier, the body often produces a protective cocktail of hormones that prevents them from feeling the full effects of pain. By the time all symptoms become present, the condition may have worsened. An primary care physician can determine the best diagnosis and treatment plan for each patient.

Learn more about our injury services

Wellness

We can also help patients stay on top of their wellness by providing women's health services, vaccinations, physicals, lab testing, and STD testing. Our goal is to keep patients healthy so they can thrive in life.

Experts recommend that everyone see the physician for a wellness exam at least once a year. These annual physicals help establish a baseline of patient health while also looking out for any warning signs of poor health. Wellness exams may also be necessary for work, school, sports, and more.

A typical wellness exam involves going over the patient's medical history, checking their vital signs, and performing some exams as necessary. These exams may include a heart exam, lung exam, head and neck exam, abdominal exam, neurological exam, dermatological exam, and extremities exam. The physician may also check the patient's general appearance for signs of illness.

Patients should remember the importance of getting annual wellness exams regardless of whether they feel they “need” them. Many health conditions can lay dormant for some time. For example, blood pressure, blood sugar, and cholesterol levels may all be high without manifesting in any symptoms. With regular screening, patients can rest assured everything is under control and monitor their health before things become too severe.

By preparing for their wellness exams ahead of time, patients can ensure that they make the most of their time with the physician. Many find it helps to bring a list of medications they are currently taking, both over-the-counter and prescribed. They may also want to bring results from any recent tests, if applicable. With regular wellness exams, patients can keep themselves in optimal health.
